entry.question:
## Physical scenario

A basketball player is standing on the floor \( 10.0 \text{ m} \) from the basket as in figure. The height of the basket is \( 3.05 \text{ m} \), and he shoots the ball at a \( 40.0^\circ \) angle with the horizontal from a height of \( 2.00 \text{ m} \).

## Question

At what speed must the player throw the basketball so that the ball goes through the hoop without striking the backboard?

## Answer choices

- A: A: \( 6.6 \text{ m/s} \)

- B: B: \( 8.2 \text{ m/s} \)

- C: C: \( 10.7 \text{ m/s} \)

- D: D: \( 2.8 \text{ m/s} \)

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image is a diagram of a basketball player shooting a ball into a hoop. On the left, a player is standing with the ball, about to shoot, at a height of 2.00 meters. The shot is at an angle of 40 degrees.

The basketball court is depicted with key lines such as the free-throw lane and the three-point line. The ball's trajectory is shown as a dotted arc, illustrating the path from the player to the hoop.

The hoop is on the right and has a height of 3.05 meters. The horizontal distance from the player to the hoop is 10.0 meters. Arrows and lines indicate these measurements, providing a clear depiction of the shooting geometry.
